content:
maria_support: heads up — multiple customers reporting 502/504s on the hosted API (/v1/generate) starting ~2026-03-15 12:08 UTC. Tickets: #2143, #2145. 

maria_support: quick sample from a customer: 
```
curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer REQ_TOKEN' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rwd-7b","prompt":"hi"}'
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
content-type: application/json
{"error":"upstream_reset", "request_id":"req_01FJ..."}
```

maria_support: triaging - who is oncall? :rotating_light:

jordan_oncall: I am oncall. I see the SLO alerts. 5xx rate jumped at 12:07 — correlates with a release. Pulling traces now.

jordan_oncall: trace id req_01FJ... shows gateway timeout to model-workers in eu-west-1, upstream: model-worker-quant-03. Error: "upstream connection reset by peer".

deploy-bot: rollout started for release r-20260315.36 -> traffic config: staged 10% -> 50% over 3m (initiated 12:06:40 UTC).

ana_platform: rollback flag/status: we flipped new routing kernel flag route_new_kernels=true at 12:06 (staged). Targeted 20% initially.

luca_release: yep, that was the staged rollout. We paused at 20% at ~12:07 to watch metrics. we saw latency climb at 12:07:30 and a small 5xx uptick then spike when it hit 25%.

kevin_eng: grabbing worker logs now. On model-worker-quant-03: 
```
[12:07:42] ERROR inference.worker - kernel mismatch: kernel v3.2 expected signature X, got Y
[12:07:43] WARN connection - dropped client conn: caused by runtime-assert in quant-op
[12:07:43] ERROR gateway - upstream reset while streaming, req=req_01FJ..., code=EPIPE
```

kevin_eng: looks like the new kernel path triggers a runtime path that crashes on certain seq-lens / quant profile. Fails under load, resets connection -> gateway 502/504.

sre_bot: alert: 5xx-rate: 7.1% (rolling 5m). Baseline 0.6%. Traffic: eu-west-1 serving 42% of requests.

maria_support: we've got two paying customers on support lines escalating. They report "requests just fail intermittently". Need a rollback ASAP and customer comms.

ops_bot: initiating emergency rollback: redwoodctl rollout abort --release r-20260315.36 --reason "upstream kernel regressions causing 5xx"

luca_release: rollback command issued at 12:10:22 UTC. Rolling back staged routing to previous config (route_new_kernels=false).

deploy-bot: rollback completed successfully at 12:10:48 UTC. Traffic back to stable release r-20260312.22.

jordan_oncall: monitoring after rollback. 5xx rate dropping... 12:11:30 -> 1.8%, 12:13:00 -> 0.7%. Looks like immediate improvement.

kevin_eng: confirmed model-worker-quant crash traces stop after rollback. We'll push a hotfix/validation to ensure kernel signature check before routing to quant path.

ana_platform: action items: 1) block automated rollouts for kernels without signature compatibility check, 2) add canary health gate: require stable 0.1% 5xx over 10m at each step, 3) add a preflight smoke test that hits seq-len edge cases.

maria_support: communicating to affected customers: "we reverted a staged config change that caused intermittent 502/504s. We’re applying extra validation; no billing impact. Reach out if you still see failures."

luca_release: postmortem draft in #postmortems, will list timeline, root cause (routing to incompatible kernel), mitigations, and follow-up owners.

jordan_oncall: leaving a note: runbook step - if a staged rollout increases 5xx >1% absolute over baseline within 5m, abort rollout and rollback to last stable.

maria_support: closing loop — customers notified, support tickets updated with workaround + apology. Thanks team. :heart:

kevin_eng: follow-up PR in review: add kernel-signature gating + smoke test harness. ETA end of day.

luca_release: we'll schedule a controlled re-release once tests pass. No forced re-rollouts until infra gating merged.

maria_support: marking incident resolved for now — will reopen if 5xx climbs again.

ops_bot: incident tagged: regression; cause: deployment-routing-flag; severity: sev2; incident_id: inc_20260315_02

maria_support: final note — good catch on the abort. quick rollback avoided larger customer impact.
